Latin word

cōnsul

cōnsul, cōnsulis m.

noun, third declension

a consul, one of the two chief magistrates of Rome; a consul, the head of a consulate

In this lexicon

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.30.1; Traupman 179, 296

Examples

  • ita Canīniō cōnsule scītō nēminem prandisse

    so, I’ll have you know, while Caninius was consul nobody had lunch (he held office for one afternoon)Cic. Fam. 7.30.1
